title: Gym Installed For Homeless Improves Their Health And Habits–Without Leaving the Shelter
text:
A gym equipment company from Finland is bringing physical fitness to the homeless community of Paris.

Inactivity is a growing public health concern, but especially in lower income communities.

To address this challenge, Omnigym installed an outdoor gym at a homeless shelter in the French capital.

They tested whether easy access to exercise would improve physical and mental wellbeing.

The project collected anonymous data from residents as well as self-assessments to evaluate the impact.

Now, one month later, Omnigym reached out to GNN to share some of their findings.

The residents were asked to assess their physical health, mental well-being, sleep, mood, and energy levels—as well as answer a few questions.

80% of respondents reported improved physical health, since the equipment arrived.

The new gym also delivered broader benefits. And respondents reported positive behavioral changes.

90% of respondents said it has helped them meet or talk to other people.

When asked what they appreciate most about the gym, one user said, “A change in behavior. I smoke less.”

Another resident simply described it as “a change” in their life, “even if only a little”.

Omnigym partnered with Emmaüs Solidarité, a French nonprofit that supports people experiencing homelessness, to pilot the courtyard fitness unit.

Kirsti Laasio, CEO of Omnigym, calls it The People’s Gym, and says the initiative addresses a need that is often overlooked.

“We want to democratize physical training and make it accessible to everyone.”
